title: Counterfactual states typically lie off the invariant set

statements.text: Because the invariant set has measure zero, a counterfactual state, a world where some experiment might have been performed but was not, typically lies off the set and is not physical. This explains quantum complementarity: non-commuting observables cannot both have well-defined outcomes.

sources.quote: counterfactual states associated with worlds where some experiment might have been performed but wasn’t, can typically lie off the invariant set
